text.p: A Pakistani court withdrew a detention order on ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband on Wednesday, but authorities simply issued a new one and kept him under arrest, a spokesman for her party said.

He said Asif Ali Zardari, investment minister in Bhutto's cabinet, was picked up from a government resthouse near Islamabad where he had been kept for three weeks since President Farooq Leghari dismissed her administration.
Zardari was taken to the southern province of Sindh, where he is from, under a new detention order, the spokesman said.
No government comment was immediately available.
The Lahore High Court had cancelled a Bhutto petition challenging Zardari's detention after a government lawyer said the original detention order had been withdrawn.
Zardari was served with another detention order from the Sindh provincial government before he could be released, the spokesman for Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) said.
"No reason was given in the order," he said. "It's the law of jungle."

No charges have been brought against Zardari and Bhutto had gone to the Lahore High Court to challenge his detention since November 5, when Leghari dismissed her government on charges of corruption and misrule, which she denies.
Soldiers seized Zardari at the governor's house in Lahore, the capital of Punjab province, where he had been staying.

The caretaker government led by Prime Minister Meraj Khalid first said Zardari, kept incommunicado for 48 hours, was being held in protective custody. Later it cited the Maintenance of Public Order ordinance to justify his detention.
The PPP spokesman said the Sindh government had also invoked the same ordinance for its detention order.
On Tuesday, Bhutto and her three children met Zardari at the resthouse near Islamabad.
In 1994, Zardari was cleared of the last of 13 similar charges brought against him after the first Bhutto government was dismissed by presidential order four years earlier.
